text.tspan: ECS Anywhere vs EKS Anywhere: containers on your own infrastructure
ECS Anywhere
AWS Region
Fully managed ECS control plane
Your data center / VMs
Server: ECS container agent + SSM agent
tasks run with launch type EXTERNAL
• Run native ECS tasks on customer-managed infrastructure
• MUST have a stable connection to the AWS Region
• Use case: compliance, regulatory, latency requirements
• Docs: no service load balancing, no service discovery, no
awsvpc, no capacity providers, no EFS; Linux only now
(Windows deprecated); SSM rotates credentials every 30 min
EKS Anywhere
Your data center (vSphere, bare metal, Nutanix, CloudStack, Snow)
Kubernetes cluster: control plane AND
workers on YOUR infrastructure
built on Amazon EKS Distro
EKS console
(via EKS Connector, optional)
• Create / operate Kubernetes clusters OUTSIDE AWS
• EKS Distro = AWS's bundled Kubernetes release
• Install with the EKS Anywhere installer (eksctl anywhere)
• Fully connected / partially disconnected: connect via
EKS Connector, use the EKS console
• Fully disconnected: EKS Distro + open-source tools
• User-managed; free, optional paid Enterprise Subscription
The difference that gets tested
• ECS Anywhere: control plane stays IN AWS; your servers only run tasks → needs a stable link to the Region.
• EKS Anywhere: the whole cluster (control plane too) runs on YOUR hardware → can run air-gapped / fully disconnected.
• EKS Hybrid Nodes (docs): control plane in AWS (EKS), worker nodes on-prem — the Kubernetes version of the ECS Anywhere idea.
• Keyword "on-premises containers + compliance / data residency / low latency, managed from AWS" → ECS Anywhere (or EKS Hybrid Nodes).
stable connection
to the Region
optional
